correctness.rationale: For all m>=4,a>=1 the exact block-coordinate vertex list consists of colored stable sets and, for odd m only, all-half colored vertices, reconstructed from block-simplex extremality and path total unimodularity. Every vertex has squared norm <= floor(m/2), strictly smaller for all-half vertices. Nonnegativity gives squared distance <=2floor(m/2); two disjoint alternating maximum independent-set vertices attain equality. Strict convexity forces all diametral endpoints to be vertices and the equality case requires disjoint coordinate support and maximum-independent-set cardinality. Counting all pairs requires enumerating two even-cycle maximum sets or m odd-cycle maximum sets with exactly m unordered pairs for each overlap size 0..r-1, plus same-support label differences. The exact formulas are derived symbolically, with 973988 exact squared distances and 111 independent combinatorial assertions passing in verify.py. Finite checks are corroborative, not a substitute for the infinite argument.

value.rationale: For a natural 2026 two-parameter family of cyclic block polytopes, the theorem gives exact full-dimensional Euclidean diameter, all extremizing endpoints, and a closed-form count of all unordered extremal pairs for all lengths and block sizes. The odd/even parity changes counting from a single uncolored diameter pair to m pairs, while colored overlaps create extra diametral pair classes; all half-integral fractional vertices are rigorously excluded. This complete rigidity/counting classification is more than a basic norm bound and supplies a geometric invariant orthogonal to the Ehrhart and transfer-matrix data.
